conventions.convention: Positive finite mode count does not impose a particle-number cutoff: the bosonic Fock space is infinite-dimensional. Ladder identities initially act on the finite-particle span.
The atom precedes the field in the completed tensor product. SI units retain positive ℏ in joule-seconds, frequencies and coupling g in inverse seconds, and dimensionless ladder operators.
AC and Countable Choice are mathematical assumptions carried from the finite-mode implementer, Fock, tensor-product and partial-trace suppliers.

The statistic g^(2)(0;ρ) is the number-distribution factorial moment divided by the squared mean; its domain requires finite strictly positive mean and finite second factorial moment. Vacuum is excluded.
The Jaynes–Cummings coupling is real g = −ℰd/ℏ, detuning is Δ = ω₀ − ω, and each excitation block has ordered basis (|e,n⟩, |g,n+1⟩), n ≥ 0. The rotating-wave scale condition is sector-dependent.
For C with columns (t,r) and (−conjugate(r),conjugate(t)), the state-action unitary fixes vacuum and sends the first creator to t a₁* + r a₂*. The first output port has η = |t|².

Pure loss uses an independently prepared vacuum second mode, nonnegative real amplitudes √η and √(1−η), and partial trace over that second mode. Complete positivity means positivity under every finite-dimensional ancilla amplification.
Number counting and homodyne are declared ideal outcome assignments; calculated distributions do not assert detector realization, measured records or empirical support.

load_bearing.statement: Adopts finitely many oscillator modes on full bosonic Fock space, a finite atomic space and algebraic-domain dipole interaction, finite implementable mode transformations, and explicitly declared ideal detector outcome models. Dynamical realizations and optional approximation regimes require their separately stated hypotheses; no laboratory realization or empirical observation is asserted.

Under the assigned two-mode model, AC and Countable Choice, the specified vacuum-fixing passive unitary maps |n,0⟩ to the binomial superposition with coefficients √binom(n,k) t^k r^(n−k). Ideal counting gives the stated binomial law, including endpoint point masses. Under the specified mode factorization, coherent input |α,0⟩ maps to |tα⟩ ⊗ |rα⟩.

For the specified one-mode, two-level rotating-wave Hamiltonian with ω,ω₀ > 0 and real g, excitation is conserved on the finite-particle core. The ground line and ordered two-dimensional excitation sectors are invariant; their eigenvalue splitting is ℏ√(Δ² + 4g²(n+1)). The prescribed squared-block-norm direct-sum realization is self-adjoint and extends the core operator.
For a one-mode density operator with ideal number probabilities p_n, finite strictly positive mean n̄ and finite m₂ = Σ n(n−1)p_n, define g^(2)(0;ρ) = m₂/n̄².

published_dependencies.used_for: Completed ordered Hilbert tensor products, elementary-tensor norms and complete product orthonormal bases under Countable Choice; supports the atom–field space and mode factorization.
Bounded tensor extensions, composition and adjoint identities, unitary tensor maps and finite-ancilla constructions; no extension of unbounded maps is inferred.
Trace-class partial trace for nonzero Hilbert factors under Countable Choice, its rank-one formula, trace-norm contraction, positivity and trace preservation.
Nuclear rank-one expansions, bounded-multiplier trace cyclicity and trace-norm limiting arguments in the loss-channel proof.
Closed creation and annihilation operators, their weighted domains and dense finite-particle domain; cited without treating the ladder operators as self-adjoint.
One-mode occupation basis, ladder coefficients and normalized coherent-state expansion; physical counting probabilities are separately assigned.
SI energy, action, time and frequency dimensions, explicit ℏ and dimensionless phases.
Declared projective outcome law, ideal measurement qualifications and finite-amplification definition of complete positivity on trace-class operators.
Adopted isolated-system evolution by the spectral exponential of the self-adjoint Jaynes–Cummings Hamiltonian in the vacuum-Rabi example.
Precise spectral-calculus meaning of U(τ) = exp(−iτH/ℏ) and vector-state evolution.
Explicit AC hypothesis carried by finite-mode implementation and spectral-calculus suppliers.
Explicit Countable Choice hypothesis carried by Fock, Hilbert tensor-product and trace-class suppliers.
